sample_unit: clinical note/BHC samples rated by 5 clinicians

links.outcome: Clinician reader preference versus automated summarization metrics for LLM-generated hospital course summaries
links.effect: Despite comparable quantitative metrics, clinicians significantly preferred GPT-4 in-context summaries over fine-tuned Llama2-13B and original summaries (P<.001), showing metrics alone missed quality differences.
links.quote: Despite comparable quantitative metrics, the reader study depicts a significant preference for summaries generated by GPT-4 with in-context learning compared to both Llama2-13B fine-tuned summaries and the original summaries (P<.001), highlighting the need for qualitative clinical evaluation.

screen.reason: Empirical study developing and benchmarking LLMs for hospital course summarization on MIMIC-IV data, evaluated via NLP metrics and a clinician reader study.
